BiblicalUsage: The cake of figs is the food of the journey and the medicine of the king: Abigail carries two hundred of them to David's men, and Hezekiah's boil is healed with a lump of figs laid on it. It is the plain, pressed provision of ordinary life, and God uses it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fig cake is the gospel of ordinary provision: God feeds His people with what is at hand, and He heals with what is pressed and plain. The plain provision is the provision God uses, and the fig cake in the hand is worth more than the feast in the dream.
